title: Are LLM Agents Behaviorally Coherent? A Latent Profiling Approach for Social Simulation
abstract: arXiv:2509.03736v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: LLM agents are increasingly proposed as substitutes for human participants in social research, usually on the strength of survey responses that match those of the humans they represent. We argue that such output-level alignment is not enough. Drawing on the behavioral sciences, we propose Latent Profiling, a framework for testing behavioral coherence: whether an agent's conversational behavior follows, as human behavioral models predict, from its own latent profile elicited by short surveys. As a case study, we test six hypotheses about preference, openness and agreement across nine open models. Agents reproduce surface-level trends but systematically fail in-depth tests: they are not behaviorally coherent, even when their individual responses look human. Latent Profiling thus offers a theory-grounded instrument for a behavioral science of LLMs.

translated_title: 大语言模型智能体在行为上是否连贯？一种面向社会模拟的潜在画像方法
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）智能体越来越多地被提议作为社会研究中人类参与者的替代品，其依据通常是它们的问卷回答与所代表的人类相匹配。我们认为这种输出层面的对齐是不够的。借鉴行为科学，我们提出了“潜在画像”，这是一个用于检验行为连贯性的框架：即智能体的对话行为是否如人类行为模型所预测的那样，源自其通过简短问卷引出的自身潜在特征。作为案例研究，我们在九个开源模型上检验了关于偏好、开放性和一致性的六个假设。结果表明，智能体能够复现表面层面的趋势，但在深度测试中却系统性地失败：它们在行为上并不连贯，即使它们的单个回答看起来很像人类。因此，潜在画像为LLM的行为科学提供了一个有理论基础的研究工具。
tldr: 论文提出“潜在画像”框架来检验LLM智能体的行为连贯性，发现九个开源模型虽能复现表面趋势，但其对话行为与自身潜在特征系统性不一致，证明仅匹配问卷回答不足以使LLM智能体替代人类参与社会研究。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Latent Profiling, a behavioral-science-grounded framework testing whether LLM agents' conversational behavior coherently follows from their survey-elicited latent profiles, revealing that nine open models reproduce surface-level trends but systematically fail in-depth behavioral coherence tests.
